baseline.method: Read exact git HEAD blobs from the existing validated publication worktree; compare current source bytes without changing either worktree or index.

currentBoundary.scope: Final recorded snapshots of the named 20 performance inputs, compared with the published baseline and bound to native-round6-5 plus build-desktop-6/player-6.
currentBoundary.laterReceiptBoundary: Native-round6-5 before/after maps and the current source freeze agree for 828 inputs; desktop build before/after maps also match. Nineteen original performance input raw hashes are unchanged; the HUD raw hash is refreshed for explicit DiscoverPanel/GravePanel coverage, with its earlier snapshot retained in sourceSnapshotHistory. Functional checks and images do not establish whole-frame speed.

claims.trigger: Any HubScreen.Build; the largest old repetition was the home page with unclaimed milestones and a visible pending-rewards row.
claims.before: BuildNavigation evaluated PendingRewards in all seven navigation iterations. BuildDeploy evaluated it twice, and a third time when the row was shown. Each PendingRewards allocated PendingAch and evaluated CollectionProgress per unclaimed milestone; the all-cards milestone also called CollectionPool for its threshold. Reward/milestone pages independently rebuilt their summary pool.
claims.after: At Build entry, derive CollectionSummary at most once: only when an unclaimed milestone needs pending eligibility, or the current milestone page actually displays progress/total. The resulting local tuple and one PendingAch list feed pending count, home row, navigation badge, reward records and milestone records through arguments. When all milestones are claimed on a page with no summary consumer, no summary pool is read. The home egg count is also reused instead of scanning stash twice.

staticCounts.homePendingEvaluationsBefore: 2, or 3 when the pending row is present
staticCounts.poolFormulaBeforePerPendingEvaluation: U + A, where U is the unclaimed-milestone count and A is 1 when the all-cards milestone is unclaimed, otherwise 0
staticCounts.conditionalExample: The checked catalog contains five milestones, including one all-cards milestone. With all five unclaimed and a positive home pending row: 10 PendingRewards evaluations × 6 CollectionPool builds = 60 summary-pool builds, plus 10 PendingAch lists. Current Build uses one summary-pool build and one PendingAch list.

claims.remainingWork: This is one Build only. When needed, it still scans/groups the current catalog and checks collected state, evaluates achievements and milestones, and creates the requested UI. Gallery/card-pool drawing may have its own necessary catalog reads. There is no cache across inventory or definition changes; claiming a milestone independently re-derives eligibility inside its transaction. The initial unconditional-summary extra read in the all-claimed/non-archive case has been removed in this round: both the published baseline and current source use 0 summary pools there. The milestone page still derives one real summary, including after all rewards were claimed; default tuples are only passed through branches with no actual summary consumer. New controlled native-source assertions cover all-claimed home/person profile at 0 provider reads and the milestone page at 1 read with the actual 1 / 2 label; the 58-assertion native Hub suite has passed with matching source inputs; timing/allocation remain unmeasured.

runtimeEvidence.scope: CurrentHubRewardsRound6Checks: one provider read where needed; all-claimed home/person at zero, milestone at one with actual 1 / 2 label; badge/reward/claim failure and revalidation behavior. Static conditional 60-to-1 example is still source-derived, not a timed benchmark.

claims.trigger: Building the selected personnel profile, upgrade or pool page.
claims.before: BuildClasses constructed a ClassSummary list for every class, read each class level/XP, constructed a ClassPool list for every class, then selected one row. The row.pool value had no live consumer in this view.
claims.after: BuildClasses reads ClassLv/ClassXP/XpForNext/LevelMax only for the selected character ruleset. The unused ClassSummary DTO/list and row.pool computation were removed. The explicit card-pool tab still constructs the selected class pool when needed for its actual cards.

staticCounts.unusedClassPoolScansBefore: C per person-page build, C = current ClassList count

claims.remainingWork: ClassLv and ClassXP still each call the existing progress lookup; actual personnel UI and selected pool cards are still rendered. The change does not claim that the entire person page has no catalog or allocation work.

runtimeEvidence.scope: CurrentHubRewardsRound6Checks: selected level/XP, no all-character class-pool projection, and all-claimed person profile zero provider reads. Total checks include the broader Hub contract suite.

claims.trigger: CurrentRunTopBar.Update while no run is active, or while coverage hides the header, including real DiscoverPanel and GravePanel owners.
claims.before: Every update walked the panel stack, tested coverage and probed both illustrated-node and reward-scene descendants, even when the header could not be shown. Three CanvasGroup visibility/interactivity properties were written every update.
claims.after: Compute run-active/coverage visibility first, with direct DiscoverPanel/GravePanel type recognition. Only a visibility transition writes the CanvasGroup properties. Hidden updates close header detail and return before illustrated/reward descendant probes; visible updates stop each category probe after finding it and stop scanning once both are found.
claims.remainingWork: When run-active and covered, Covered still scans up to P panels and retains the settings-component check. Explicit discovery/grave coverage prevents the global HUD from covering those titles and lets these covered frames use the same early return. Visible frames retain coverage/classification, value comparisons and health animation. No whole-page O(1), zero-draw or measured-speed claim is made.

runtimeEvidence.scope: CurrentHudRound6Checks: real settings coverage, hidden numeric/scene state remains deferred, unhide reads current values. Exact avoided probe/property-call counts remain static source evidence, not runtime instrumentation.

additionalCoverage.scope: Includes real grave owner/header CanvasGroup alpha 0 and restored alpha 1 checks. The fresh native total is 369; no probe-count runtime instrumentation or benchmark is inferred.

claims.trigger: An eligible key-down frame after the existing anyKeyDown/IME guard, with no active key-rebinding capture owner.
claims.before: PollKeys scanned the cached KeyCode array for capture before scanning it again for normal actions. A pressed capture candidate could be converted to its binding name once in the guard and again in CaptureKey.
claims.after: The capture pass runs only while SuppressGameplayInput says a capture owner exists. Captured keys compute the binding name once and pass it to TryCapture. The existing second owner check still prevents gameplay dispatch if capture remains active.

staticCounts.ordinaryActionPass: retained when eligible; text fields can still return early

claims.remainingWork: The KeyCode array was already statically cached; this does not eliminate per-frame Enum allocation because none was present. Frames with no key-down were already skipped. IME, modifier keys, input focus, Escape, Space and Enter keep their existing gates. The retired uncalled DiagClick body was removed; no runtime-speed benefit is assigned to deleting an uncalled method.

runtimeEvidence.scope: Static source comparison only; none of the bound native/Source receipts directly exercises the absence-of-capture KeyCode pass count or physical keyboard input.

claims.trigger: Preparing a map-item discovery whose existing receipt is valid for the current authoritative card catalog.
claims.before: Even an existing receipt entered TryPersistMutation, capturing whole-run/Base/RNG/extraction/battle state, cloning the profile transaction, serializing Base/run and committing a profile write. Pool eligibility was rebuilt for each saved candidate; final projection performed per-ID catalog lookup.
claims.after: Build the current CardLibrary pool and ID dictionary once. Validate/project an existing receipt through that dictionary and return without a mutation transaction or write. First generation still uses the existing transaction and rolls back receipt/RNG on failure; final selection still validates and commits through the existing transaction.
claims.remainingWork: Every reopen still constructs the current pool/list/dictionary and checks source ownership, read-error gate and all saved candidate IDs. It is not a persistent cache, and malformed/missing-definition receipts remain failures rather than silently rerolling. Comparing authoritative eligibility also changes correctness for custom overrides; this is not merely a faster read of the obsolete static catalog.

runtimeEvidence.scope: RunRound6Checks: existing candidates reopen under a real file lock; provider reads one, SaveCompleted zero, state/profile/RNG unchanged. First/final checkpoints and failure behavior remain tested.

claims.trigger: The retained coin-pickup command path when pickupClaimed and pickupSaved are already true; the normal claim-then-leave consumer passes no onDone callback.
claims.before: PickupScreen.Claim saved the claim checkpoint, then TryLeaveCurrentPickup entered another full mutation/save transaction solely to set the runtime Phase to idle.
claims.after: The already-saved branch sets runtime Phase=idle and returns without a second transaction/write. Failed/unsaved claims still retry the real checkpoint before leaving; unclaimed leave keeps its existing save. CaptureRunSave does not serialize Phase and LoadRun re-enters idle.
claims.reachabilityBoundary: Current new layered maps do not generate coin/wood/rations/key nodes. This is a retained command/developer-constructed coin-receipt path, not a claimed performance gain for normal new-map coin visits. No third FinishNode write is assumed: the actual RunLoopBridge consumer supplies onDone=null.
claims.remainingWork: The original claim persistence and failure receipt remain. Claim settlement still credits coins before attempting its checkpoint and retains that memory state on save failure; this change does not add an invented rollback/refund.

runtimeEvidence.scope: RunRound6Checks: controlled coin receipt, one claim checkpoint, locked-profile leave changes only runtime phase, no second SaveCompleted/write, retries/load retained. This is not natural new-map coin-node coverage.

claims.trigger: Selecting or unselecting a still-current, unchanged sacrifice candidate.
claims.before: The name-only candidate button changed the selection HashSet and called Rebuild, clearing/rebuilding the node body/footer and every candidate row on each click.
claims.after: Mounted candidate controls are keyed by actual UID. A valid unchanged Toggle updates its selection mark, state text, selected-count text and confirm availability, while preserving the candidate/root/scroll view. AlignCandidates reconciles added/removed UIDs and refreshes a face only when its serialized definition changes.
claims.remainingWork: Each Toggle still calls GetSacrificeCandidates: an O(N) owned-card eligibility scan plus a new list, then a linear UID search and serialization of the selected current card for stale-definition validation. Text and selection-mark changes can dirty UI; this is not zero redraw or zero GC. AlignCandidates still scans/reconciles candidates, serializes definitions and rebinds events; confirm also revalidates the whole candidate set.
claims.necessaryAddedWork: Unlike the old name-only rows, the new page mounts real CardFace controls with fees and descriptions. That initial drawing and required changed-definition refresh are intentional fidelity/correctness work, not removed cost. The report makes no total page-time or memory comparison between the old text-only view and the new illustrated view.

runtimeEvidence.scope: CurrentSacrificeRound6Checks: exact Button/CardFace/scroll-content/offset identity retained across pick/retract, and retained view after failed persistence with owner/UID validation. No zero-GC or frame-time assertion.
